text: You look up tonight, and it's just not there. No warning. Bro really said, "I'm out."
So what happens to us? Are we cooked?
First, the oceans take an L.
The Moon's gravity tugs on Earth's water. That's what makes the tides rise and fall.
The Sun pulls too, so tides wouldn't vanish. But they'd shrink to less than half their size.
Weaker tides mean weaker currents along the coast. And those currents stir up the food sea life depends on.
Tide pools take a hit too. The crabs and snails living there could lose places to feed and breed.
Then there are animals that set their clocks by the Moon.
Many corals use moonlight to pick one big night to spawn. Thousands release their eggs at the same time.
No Moon, no signal. Their timing could fall apart.
And the nights? Way darker. A full Moon is around a hundred times brighter than starlight.
But the biggest job the Moon has? It keeps Earth's tilt steady.
That tilt gives us our seasons. Without the Moon, it could wobble a lot more over millions of years.
So the seasons could slowly swing to extremes. Earth's climate, on shuffle. Not a vibe.
Don't panic, though. Earth won't fly off into space, and it won't stop spinning.
So maybe stop taking the Moon for granted. Bro's been carrying Earth this whole time.
